name: Ganvié lake village
subtitle: Ganvié is a village of stilt houses on Lake Nokoué, about 30 km from Cotonou, where residents move by boat.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: About 30 km from Cotonou, on Lake Nokoué

facts.label: Movement
facts.value: Buildings sit on stilts; residents travel by boat

facts.label: Name and origin
facts.value: Name means 'we survived'; refuge in the 18th century for people escaping slave raids

facts.label: Slave raiders
facts.value: Armed men from the Fon and Dahomey kingdoms captured people and sold them to Portuguese traders

facts.label: Founders
facts.value: Founded by the Tofinu, a fishing people living on the Benin coast before the 17th century

facts.label: Pressure on the lake
facts.value: Water hyacinth competes with fish, which are also threatened by backfill, pollution and overfishing

facts.label: Water hyacinth project
facts.value: 75 tons harvested and over 1,000 young people trained, in an AFD-supported programme

facts.label: Heritage status
facts.value: Council of Ministers decree of 4 March 2026 classifies the Cité lacustre de Ganvié as national cultural heritage

parts.text: Ganvié is a village of stilt houses on Lake Nokoué, about 30 km from Cotonou, where residents move by boat. Its name is said to mean 'we survived', and it served as a refuge from slave raids by the Fon and Dahomey kingdoms. Fishing is still the main livelihood, but water hyacinth, backfill, pollution and overfishing now pressure the lake; in March 2026 the government classified the site as national cultural heritage.
